sigma_nuclei_redshift.png.title: Initial shear comparison - nuclear inventories versus redshift
sigma_nuclei_redshift.png.what_to_read: Compare each of the eight isotope panels separately; horizontal reservoir lines and tiny radioactive stocks have different physical origins. Redshift decreases to the right; the upper Myr axis is the named reference clock, not every curve's clock.
sigma_nuclei_redshift.png.physical_interpretation: Initial shear increases from zero to 0.6 while both initial stress norms remain zero. Stable totals overlap because they are passive reservoirs; T and neutrons are separately propagated creation-minus-loss inventories.
sigma_nuclei_redshift.png.nuclear_astro_context: The stable nuclear reservoirs remain inherited inputs. Shear changes reaction exposure, not the DD tunnelling coefficient at a fixed gas temperature.
sigma_nuclei_redshift.png.claim_limit: This is a prescribed-temperature, prescribed-UV comparison, not a self-consistent heating or primordial nucleosynthesis calculation. T/n totals assume immediate thermalization and bare reactants.

sigma_ions_redshift.png.title: Initial shear comparison - ionic inventories versus redshift
sigma_ions_redshift.png.what_to_read: Follow charge states within each isotope panel; the ordinate is absolute nuclei per baryon rather than the fraction of that isotope. Redshift decreases to the right; the upper Myr axis is the named reference clock, not every curve's clock.
sigma_ions_redshift.png.physical_interpretation: Initial shear increases from zero to 0.6 while both initial stress norms remain zero. Ionization moves nuclei between charge states while recombination returns them; neither process changes the total number of that isotope.
sigma_ions_redshift.png.nuclear_astro_context: H/D and paired He/Li isotopes share electronic fractions here; their inherited nuclear inventories differ. T charge states remain unresolved.

sigma_ionic_difference_redshift.png.title: Initial shear comparison - charge-fraction response versus redshift
sigma_ionic_difference_redshift.png.what_to_read: Read signed changes from the matched zero anchor at common redshift, using the stated linear region of the symmetric logarithmic axis. Redshift decreases to the right; the upper Myr axis is the named reference clock, not every curve's clock.
sigma_ionic_difference_redshift.png.physical_interpretation: Shear changes the expansion rate and time available for reactions; generated stresses subsequently respond. A positive entry means a larger conditional charge fraction at the same redshift, not necessarily at the same elapsed time.

sigma_stress_redshift.png.title: Initial shear comparison - dynamical mechanism versus redshift
sigma_stress_redshift.png.what_to_read: Read signed shear, separate matter/photon/neutrino stresses, relative expansion and elapsed time together, retaining the signs that norms would erase. Redshift decreases to the right; the upper Myr axis is the named reference clock, not every curve's clock.
sigma_stress_redshift.png.physical_interpretation: Shear changes the expansion rate and time available for reactions; generated stresses subsequently respond. sigma_stress_redshift.png.nuclear_astro_context: The stable nuclear reservoirs remain inherited inputs. Shear changes reaction exposure, not the DD tunnelling coefficient at a fixed gas temperature.

strong_pi_m/strong_pi_m_ions_elapsed_tim.physical_interpretation: Initial matter stresses zero, 0.01, 0.05 and 0.1 share the new component density and mean pressure. Ionization moves nuclei between charge states while recombination returns them; neither process changes the total number of that isotope.
strong_pi_m/strong_pi_m_ions_elapsed_tim.nuclear_astro_context: H/D and paired He/Li isotopes share electronic fractions here; their inherited nuclear inventories differ. T charge states remain unresolved.
strong_pi_m/strong_pi_m_ions_elapsed_tim.claim_limit: Use the new hot zero anchor. This is a distinct conditional component family, not a continuation of the cold model or an observational fit. The inherited atomic curves and conditional neutron total are separate model outputs.

strong_pi_m/strong_pi_m_ionic_difference.title: Stronger matched matter-stress family - charge-fraction response versus redshift
strong_pi_m/strong_pi_m_ionic_difference.what_to_read: Read signed changes from the matched zero anchor at common redshift, using the stated linear region of the symmetric logarithmic axis. Redshift decreases to the right; the upper Myr axis is the named reference clock, not every curve's clock.
strong_pi_m/strong_pi_m_ionic_difference.physical_interpretation: The stronger component generates a fraction response separated from the observed control discrepancy, approximately quadratic in the tested initial stress. A positive entry means a larger conditional charge fraction at the same redshift, not necessarily at the same elapsed time.
strong_pi_m/strong_pi_m_ionic_difference.nuclear_astro_context: A visible lithium fraction shift need not dominate the electron inventory, because lithium is rare. Nuclear conversion is not inferred from a charge-fraction difference.
strong_pi_m/strong_pi_m_ionic_difference.claim_limit: Use the new hot zero anchor. This is a distinct conditional component family, not a continuation of the cold model or an observational fit.

strong_pi_m/strong_pi_m_stress_redshift..title: Stronger matched matter-stress family - dynamical mechanism versus redshift
strong_pi_m/strong_pi_m_stress_redshift..what_to_read: Read signed shear, separate matter/photon/neutrino stresses, relative expansion and elapsed time together, retaining the signs that norms would erase. Redshift decreases to the right; the upper Myr axis is the named reference clock, not every curve's clock.
strong_pi_m/strong_pi_m_stress_redshift..physical_interpretation: The stronger component generates a fraction response separated from the observed control discrepancy, approximately quadratic in the tested initial stress. The stress source competes with expansion damping. Its accumulated geometric response determines the clock entering the atomic rate equation.
strong_pi_m/strong_pi_m_stress_redshift..nuclear_astro_context: The semi-relativistic component is nonbaryonic; its momentum scale is not the gas temperature. Nuclear reactants still use the prescribed gas history.
strong_pi_m/strong_pi_m_stress_redshift..claim_limit: Use the new hot zero anchor. This is a distinct conditional component family, not a continuation of the cold model or an observational fit.

strong_pi_m/strong_pi_m_control_comparis.title: Strong matter response compared with its refined control
strong_pi_m/strong_pi_m_control_comparis.what_to_read: Compare the strongest nominal and refined results and their signed residuals. Symmetric logarithmic axes preserve zero and signs; the upper clock uses the matched hot zero reference.
strong_pi_m/strong_pi_m_control_comparis.physical_interpretation: The ionic response is about 5.46e-6, while the largest nominal/control fraction discrepancy is 2.31e-10. The leading peak keeps its sign after refinement, separating this response from the observed discretization change.
strong_pi_m/strong_pi_m_control_comparis.nuclear_astro_context: This tests the expansion and atomic solver, not the accuracy of extrapolated fusion coefficients. A better numerical control cannot validate fast-neutron thermalization or nuclear charge injection.
strong_pi_m/strong_pi_m_control_comparis.claim_limit: One combined refinement is an observed discrepancy, not a rigorous global error bound or empirical uncertainty interval. It does not establish a detection threshold below the smallest tested stress.

../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.title: Archived strong-case shear and stress magnitudes
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.what_to_read: Read the shear above and the separate stress magnitudes below for one strong positive-shear case. The original lower time axis is in Gyr; the upper redshift axis describes that same trajectory.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.physical_interpretation: Expansion damps dimensional shear while the signed stresses can replenish it. Magnitudes alone cannot show whether matter and radiation reinforce or oppose one another, so the separate signed-history figure is needed.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.nuclear_astro_context: The matter stress belongs to a nonbaryonic collisionless component. Its relevance to reionization is the expansion clock, not direct nuclear heating or a change of reaction constants.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.claim_limit: This archived atomic-only diagnostic contains no nuclear source calculation. Its single-case clock must not be transferred to the newer multi-case comparison plots.

../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.title: Archived initial-stress plane and final signed shear
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.what_to_read: Each panel contains fifteen measured cases at one initial shear magnitude. Position gives actual initial signed matter and radiation stresses; color gives final signed shear. Read each colorbar independently.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.physical_interpretation: Changing either stress can alter the net shear source, and opposed signs can reduce it. The grid shows discrete attained solutions, not a continuous stability boundary or an interpolated probability map.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.nuclear_astro_context: The map identifies geometric histories that later weight atomic and nuclear reaction exposure. It does not display isotope synthesis, nuclear cross sections, or a baryonic pressure quadrupole.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.claim_limit: Color scales span each panel separately. Equal colors in different panels need not mean equal final shear, and the finite grid does not cover every positive distribution.

../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.title: Archived atomic-only isotope census versus redshift
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.what_to_read: Follow positive ionic abundances as redshift decreases. Each curve counts a particular isotope and charge per baryon; empty panels and annotations report the original model's unpopulated entries.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.physical_interpretation: UV ionization redistributes a fixed nuclear reservoir among charge states, while recombination depends on the electron density. H1 and D share electronic fractions but differ greatly in absolute abundance; helium and lithium isotope pairs behave similarly.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.nuclear_astro_context: The archived T and neutron zeros were imposed by missing initial inventories and nuclear sources. They are superseded as nuclear predictions by the later positive-source audit, not erased from the historical record.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.claim_limit: The figure retains its original display and atomic-only scope. It cannot determine tritium production or its unresolved daughter charge partition.

../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.title: Archived atomic-only isotope census versus elapsed time
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.what_to_read: Read the same strong-case ionic census against elapsed Gyr from z=20. Positive curves use logarithmic abundance; zeros are annotated rather than placed at an invented plotting floor.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.physical_interpretation: The clock reveals how long the gas spends ionizing or recombining, whereas the redshift companion emphasizes expansion stage. These are different coordinates of one saved trajectory, not separate reaction experiments.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.nuclear_astro_context: Stable H, D, He and Li nuclei are inherited reservoirs. Changes in their ionic curves do not mean new nuclei were manufactured. Archived T and neutron zeros reflect the missing nuclear layer.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.claim_limit: Do not compare its Gyr labels directly with newer Myr labels without conversion. The old charge calculation supplies no newly produced tritium charge history.

../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.title: Archived nine conditional charge fractions
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.what_to_read: Within each H, He or Li panel, read the fractions among that element's charge states, rather than absolute isotope abundances. Their sum remains one. Time is in the original Gyr display.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.physical_interpretation: More ionizing photons move weight toward higher charges; increasing electron density strengthens recombination. The selected spectrum reaches He II ionization but stops below Li II and Li III thresholds, leaving initially empty higher lithium states unpopulated.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.nuclear_astro_context: These are electronic transitions, not changes in nuclear mass number. Equal-element rates explain the shared H1/D, He3/He4 and Li6/Li7 conditional histories.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.claim_limit: The quotient assumes equal operators and initial fractions. It cannot automatically assign these fractions to tritium injected by a new nuclear reaction.

../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.title: Archived strong-case signed stress decomposition
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.what_to_read: Compare signed matter, photon, neutrino and total stresses above with signed shear below. Unlike a norm plot, this keeps positive and negative orientations and exposes cancellations.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.physical_interpretation: The displayed strong positive-shear case combines positive matter and negative radiation input. Photon scattering and neutrino free streaming produce different subsequent histories, so the total source cannot be reconstructed by adding positive magnitudes.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.nuclear_astro_context: This mechanism changes the expansion interval available for atomic transitions and any later passive nuclear postprocessing. It does not make the UV source harder or alter nuclear penetration factors.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.claim_limit: This is one selected mixed-parameter trajectory in the old atomic model. Its changing stress is not an observational polarization prediction or an independent single-axis derivative.

../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.title: Archived cancellation with negative matter and positive radiation
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.what_to_read: Follow the signed components from their initially cancelling state. This first cancellation example has negative matter stress and positive radiation stress, with zero initial shear; the original time axis is in Gyr.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.physical_interpretation: A vanishing initial sum does not mean each component vanishes. Their distinct evolution changes the sum and can generate shear later, so cancellation is an initial condition rather than a conservation law.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.nuclear_astro_context: The changing geometry can alter reaction exposure even when the initial total stress is zero. Nuclear target abundances and local rate coefficients remain separate physical inputs.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.claim_limit: This curve does not imply that all opposite-stress configurations evolve identically. The original atomic-only run contains no nuclear creation term and uses prescribed thermal and UV histories.

../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.title: Archived cancellation with positive matter and negative radiation
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.what_to_read: Read the second initially cancelling configuration, now with positive matter and negative radiation stress. Track the small total alongside the larger components and the generated signed shear.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.physical_interpretation: Reversing component orientations changes the trajectory because matter and radiation do not redshift or interact identically. An initially zero shear source therefore need not remain zero, and exact cancellation cannot be inferred from rounded filename amplitudes.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.nuclear_astro_context: For nuclear applications, this is a changed geometric clock, not a cancellation of nuclear reaction probabilities. Positive collision event rates do not cancel merely because macroscopic stresses have opposite signs.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.claim_limit: Only this chosen distribution and initial state are shown. Its historical Gyr clock and atomic-only scope remain distinct from the new all-bare conditional nuclear layer.

../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.title: Archived negative shear with zero initial sector stresses
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.what_to_read: Read the negative signed-shear trajectory and the stresses it generates from initially isotropic matter and radiation sectors. Retain the signs rather than comparing only their positive norms.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.physical_interpretation: Directional expansion can produce anisotropic pressures even when those pressures initially vanish. Equal positive and negative shear norms give the same initial shear-squared energy term, but do not guarantee identical later pressure histories.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.nuclear_astro_context: This illustrates an indirect pathway to different ionization exposure. It does not reverse a nuclear reaction, exchange T with He3, or change the sign of a microscopic event rate.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.claim_limit: The figure is an archived orientation control, not a symmetry proof. The gas temperature and soft UV are prescribed, and nuclear channels were absent from its atomic evolution.

../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.title: Archived negative shear with opposed sector stresses
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.what_to_read: Compare negative initial shear with the positive matter and negative radiation contributions retained in this mixed case. The upper panel resolves their sum; the lower panel follows the resulting signed shear.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.physical_interpretation: The initial stress source can support or oppose the existing shear depending on sign. Photon and neutrino components subsequently separate, so the outcome depends on the evolving balance rather than initial norms alone.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.nuclear_astro_context: The relevance to nuclear astrophysics is the available time at each density and temperature, not an intrinsic orientation dependence of the adopted unpolarized nuclear coefficients.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.claim_limit: Several initial quantities distinguish this trajectory from the zero-stress negative-shear example. It is not a controlled derivative with respect to shear alone or a complete coupled nuclear calculation.

../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.title: Archived numerical controls for the atomic pilot
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.what_to_read: Read the absolute differences between each selected nominal L16 trajectory and its tighter L24 counterpart at the same saved redshift index. The horizontal line is the original acceptance ceiling, not a measured error bar.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.physical_interpretation: Small discrepancies show stability under these particular numerical changes. The actual fraction discrepancy is far more informative for tiny response claims than merely staying below a much looser acceptance ceiling.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.nuclear_astro_context: Reliable atomic histories provide backgrounds for nuclear postprocessing, but numerical agreement cannot validate nuclear extrapolations, primordial abundances or omitted transport. The original cold matter-only response is smaller than the observed fraction discrepancy.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.claim_limit: Three selected controls do not prove convergence uniformly over every parameter or state. Absolute differences discard sign and should not be read as physical source terms.

../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.title: Archived prescribed thermal and UV energy bookkeeping
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.what_to_read: Read the imposed temperature first, the signed required exchanges second, and the explicitly labelled energy ratios last. Positive and negative powers distinguish energy supply from removal; they are not negative physical temperatures.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.physical_interpretation: Maintaining the prescribed thermal history requires energy as the gas expands and its particle count and binding energy change. The plotted remaining bath-minus-escape term is a bookkeeping requirement, not an independently solved astrophysical heating mechanism.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.nuclear_astro_context: Nuclear reaction Q would need consistent deposition, recoil and escaping-particle accounting before entering this budget. Small test-fluid energy ratios do not by themselves establish correct nuclear heating.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.claim_limit: Temperature is an input. The denominators distinguish material/radiation energy from cosmological-constant and shear terms; these ratios must not be mistaken for a closed thermal-feedback solution.

../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.title: Archived strong mixed case relative to the isotropic baseline
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.what_to_read: Read signed shear and stress differences, the largest conditional charge-fraction difference, and the two elapsed clocks at common redshift. The time curves are displayed separately because the trajectories do not share a clock.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.physical_interpretation: The strong mixed case changes geometry and the time available for the same prescribed atomic rates. The fraction response is therefore a geometric and exposure effect within this closure, rather than a changed ionization cross section.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.nuclear_astro_context: Such clock differences can change cumulative nuclear events even when local late-time radioactive balances nearly coincide. This archived figure itself, however, contains no nuclear source calculation.
../rei_isotope_quotient_pilot_20261022/p.claim_limit: This comparison changes multiple initial parameters and is not one of the newer independent-axis slices. Its fraction difference is at common redshift, not common elapsed time.

../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.title: Archived direct deuterium-fusion source diagnostic
../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.what_to_read: Read prescribed temperature above and the logarithmic DD-to-T and DD-to-neutron sources below as redshift decreases. Source values are births per baryon per second, not accumulated abundances.
../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.physical_interpretation: Rising temperature strongly increases Coulomb penetration in the conditional Maxwellian integral. The source also contains density and the square of the available deuterium-ion fraction, so temperature alone does not determine its time history.
../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.nuclear_astro_context: The two DD branches create T+p and He3+n. Their finite log sources demonstrate positive production under the selected low-energy continuation, even when linear floating-point values would underflow.
../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.claim_limit: This is the earlier ionized-deuterium DD lane, not the later all-bare full network. Constant-S continuation and a thermal reactant distribution are conditional assumptions, not empirical validation at these temperatures.

../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.title: Archived direct tritium births and surviving inventory
../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.what_to_read: Compare cumulative T births and DD-neutron births with the surviving direct T stock and its local quasi-steady estimate. All are baryon-normalized, but cumulative births and surviving nuclei answer different questions.
../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.physical_interpretation: Birth counts keep every production event, whereas the stock loses T by beta decay. When the source changes slowly compared with the lifetime, the stock follows roughly source divided by decay rate rather than the entire accumulated history.
../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.nuclear_astro_context: A 12.312-year half-life is short compared with a Myr-scale reionization interval. Very small survivors therefore coexist with a much larger cumulative production count, without violating baryon bookkeeping.
../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.claim_limit: The quasi-steady curve is a limiting interpretation of the earlier DD-only model. It is not an exact initial-time solution or the complete coupled capture/decay network.

../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.title: Archived conditional full-network T and neutron stocks
../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.what_to_read: Read T and free-neutron logarithmic inventories on the same per-baryon scale. Initial zeros are omitted from that logarithmic ordinate; the curves represent surviving nuclei propagated directly in the fast subsystem.
../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.physical_interpretation: Production competes with radioactive decay and capture. Short loss times make late stocks respond to local conditions rather than preserve every historical birth, explaining their near-overlap across backgrounds with common temperature and density.
../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.nuclear_astro_context: The network includes direct DD production and secondary neutron routes. Its tiny inventories are negligible compared with inherited D, helium and lithium reservoirs in this particular conditional calculation.
../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.claim_limit: Bare reactants and instantaneous thermalization are assumed. The plotted illustrative case was selected numerically; roundoff-scale endpoint differences are not a physical ranking, and no T ionic partition is supplied.

../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.title: Archived tritium production channels
../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.what_to_read: Compare logarithmic cumulative T births by reaction route. The endpoints of the horizontal marks carry the values; the arbitrary left origin of each segment is not zero production.
../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.physical_interpretation: DD dominates because deuterium is available, whereas secondary channels require the exceedingly scarce neutron population. A large thermal He3-neutron coefficient cannot overcome the lack of projectiles. Li6 and deuterium neutron captures are further restricted by targets and competing losses.
../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.nuclear_astro_context: These are integrated births, not surviving T. Nuclear stoichiometry differs among routes even when each produces one tritium nucleus; the full event ledger also tracks consumed reactants and outgoing particles.
../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.claim_limit: The figure shows selected routes above its display cutoff. Much smaller finite reverse contributions remain in the ledger; absence here is not an exact zero or permission to omit a channel.

../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.title: Archived radioactive stocks against time and gas temperature
../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.what_to_read: The left panel uses actual elapsed Gyr of one saved trajectory; the right uses that trajectory's prescribed gas temperature. These are two horizontal coordinates of the same T and neutron stock history.
../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.physical_interpretation: Temperature changes the charged-particle source exponentially through tunnelling, while the available proper time controls accumulation and loss. Near a temperature plateau, density can continue falling and the stock can change even when temperature barely moves.
../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.nuclear_astro_context: This distinguishes a source-temperature correlation from a universal abundance function of temperature. Short-lived T and neutrons reflect the combined source, density and hazard history, unlike the largely fixed stable nuclear reservoirs.
../rei_tritium_production_audit_20261022.claim_limit: Temperature was not obtained from nuclear heating. The archived display retains Gyr and log10 ordinate labels; it must not be read as a new thermal-feedback solution or empirical production prediction.
